paper_title: The State of the Art in Constraining Axion-to-Nucleon Coupling and Non-Newtonian Gravity from Laboratory Experiments
suggested_experiment_name: Laboratory review: magnetometer / Cavendish-type / Casimir-less / molecular-hydrogen constraints on axion-nucleon coupling
notes: This is a review article (Mostepanenko & Klimchitskaya, Universe 2020, arXiv:2009.04517) summarizing previously published constraints on axion-to-nucleon coupling g_an^2/(4pi) and Yukawa-type non-Newtonian gravity from Casimir force measurements, Casimir-less experiments, magnetometer measurements, Cavendish-type experiments, and molecular hydrogen beams. It presents no new original limits; all constraints are reproduced from earlier works (e.g. refs [26,37,56,57,76,77]). Constraints appear only as figure lines (Figures 6 and 8) with no numerical tables or explicit coupling values in the text, so no data points could be extracted. The relevant coupling is the generic axion-nucleon coupling (paper assumes g_an = g_ap), plotted as g_an^2/(4pi) vs axion mass from ~1e-10 eV to 200 eV; constraints derive from two-axion exchange (GUT axions).
